0.comment: Yae Miko: Ei, the Raiden Shogun
0.content:
Yae Miko calls herself Ei's familiar and servant, and is one of her only friends who survived the ravages of time. Ei once knew her as a youngster "who could easily be swayed with some Fried Tofu" and is relieved to see her grow so shrewd. When Ei withdrew into the Plane of Euthymia, she gave Yae the Electro Gnosis. Yae watched for centuries and finally used the Traveler to reach her. In the Plane she told Ei that her eternity had made her suffer as much as anyone. Ei agreed to end the Vision Hunt Decree. Yae calls her by name and teases her constantly; in her 2026 birthday letter she wrote that Ei "thinks far too much, and allows herself to accept far too little".

Ei admits she was a little upset to be the target of Yae's scheming and plans to "strike her first" next time, though she expects Yae to dodge. During Transient Dreams (2.5), when Ei went through a torii beneath the shrine to confront the rebelling Shogun puppet, she sent the Traveler back to tell Yae to govern Inazuma in her stead, and Yae reactivated the torii so the Traveler could rejoin her. Since then Yae has shown Ei modern Inazuma and her own publisher's light novels.

1.comment: Yae Miko: Kitsune Saiguu and the Hakushin kitsune
1.content:
The Kitsune Saiguu, of the Hakushin lineage, once headed the Grand Narukami Shrine and was one of Ei's closest companions. She doted on the young Yae, who perched on her shoulder at the youkai's storytelling feasts. In the cataclysm five hundred years ago, monsters attacked Inazuma while both Archons were away. Saiguu led the defence and was consumed by the darkness. Yae remembers only that Saiguu said she was going on a long trip and never came back, and that she talked her into being Guuji by promising all the fried tofu she wanted. "That woman spoke so much nonsense."

Remnants of Saiguu's memory later appeared in the Sacred Sakura's roots as the masked shrine maiden Hanachirusato, who helped the Traveler with the cleansing ritual. Yae followed Saiguu to the youkai's Mikawa Flower Festival one year and watched her play Akitsu Haneasobi.

2.comment: Yae Miko: The Electro Gnosis and the Balladeer
2.content:
After Ei made her Shogun puppet she had nowhere to keep her Gnosis, so she left it with Yae at the shrine. Ei expected Yae might "sell" it, but only for something equally valuable. When the Traveler fell to the Balladeer's Tatarigami trap at the Delusion factory, Yae rescued them by giving him the Gnosis. She judged the trade a good one: the Gnosis was useless to Ei and a source of conflict, and the Traveler was the core of her plan. She later revealed that the Balladeer was Ei's first prototype puppet, sealed instead of destroyed, then augmented by the Fatui.

Yae says she warned Ei the puppet was a disaster waiting to happen. Ei would not lift a finger against her own creation, and Yae would have disposed of it herself had she known. Of the present she says only, "we're no longer waiting for the disaster to happen." The Wanderer calls her a smooth-talking youkai who pretends to care about humans to please her god. A web event recapping the Gnoses before Version 7.0 (Snezhnaya Awaits, 2026) quotes her line "I handed that over."

3.comment: Yae Miko: The Plan to Save Ei
3.content:
Yae was interested in the Traveler because Ei had let them into the Plane of Euthymia, the first person in centuries. She put the Traveler through grueling training and invited Kujou Sara to the shrine. With help from Ayaka, Thoma, Yoimiya and Sayu, she produced proof that Kujou Takayuki had falsified war reports and dealt with the Fatui. Sara turned on him. Yae gave the Traveler an omamori with "vague promises". During the Traveler's duel with Ei it let her enter the Plane. She reminded the Traveler whose wishes they fought for, the confiscated Visions lit the realm, and Ei lost. Afterwards Yae persuaded her to rethink eternity.

At the end (Wishes) Yae answered the Traveler's questions about the Shogun puppet, the twin Archons, their sibling and Sumeru. She suggested the Traveler might lack a Vision because they have not yet found an ambition that "shines in unison with fate itself". Then she asked whether that had all got a little heavy.

4.content:
Yae founded Yae Publishing House in Hanamizaka, Inazuma City, because she wanted to read more interesting light novels. She found that watching frazzled authors invent excuses for deadline extensions is the real fun. It runs the "This Novel Is Amazing!" contest, publishes authors from beyond Inazuma such as Zhenyu (Xingqiu) and Chang the Ninth, and is described as a giant of the industry. Yae is its boss, founder and final editor. Her staff treat her as intimidating.

Its founding money came from the Fire-Soothing Festival Committee, whose budget Yae redirected from shrine dances into a novel contest. She believes gods and great beings die and their tales are lost unless skilled writers record them, so she wants to "cultivate" home-grown talent. She keeps trying to sign the Traveler to write their adventures.

key: A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits
5.content: In her Story Quest, a book of summoning rituals swept Inazuma. Wishes seemed to come true, but people started acting strangely, and the book was hurting her sales. Yae exorcised a possessed swordsman in Konda Village, had the Traveler's travels turned into a rival novel, and traced the book to the lingering memory of her old friend Urakusai. He had been stirred from the Sacred Sakura's roots when Rifthounds damaged them, and meant no harm: he wanted the youkai memories to enjoy life once more and leave without regret. He asked after her, and she said she was content and that even Ei had changed. At his wish she held one last Hyakkiyakou at the shrine, guiding the faded youkai into the sky.

6.content: Centuries ago Yae and the yumekui-baku Mizuki were neighbours. Yae had just learned human form and let Mizuki taste her dreams. Mizuki later left Inazuma. On her return she avoided Yae's eyes in the street, which Yae enjoyed watching. They are now rivals. Mizuki criticises Yae Publishing House in the "That's Life" reader column, and Yae threatens to write "The Baku Chronicles" herself. In Mizuki's Story Quest (5.4), Yae urged her to sell her bathhouse shares, then quietly gave the Traveler Emura Chuuya's address, asking them not to say where it came from. Mizuki thanked her at the end and admitted she feels inferior to her. Yae admitted she would have acted more directly if she had not feared upsetting Mizuki.

7.comment: Yae Miko: The Kamisato siblings and the Raiden Gokaden affair
7.content: When the Raiden Gokaden conspiracy implicated the Kamisato Clan, Yae, who normally avoids government, interceded with the Shogun and saved them from dismissal. She held secret talks with the clan head and told them they survived "only due to the Shogun's mercy". The Kamisato remembered, and in the storm of the Vision Hunt they stayed loyal to the Shogun. Ayato says she has been kind to the clan but never liked him personally. She calls him "the Yashiro rascal" and was unpredictable even as a child. Yae adores Ayaka, says she would have hired her if she weren't a Kamisato, and gets her to cook lunch for her.

8.comment: Yae Miko: Gorou, Sara and the tengu
8.content: Gorou cannot bear to discuss her. In his Hangout Event (2.3) he trained to stop being afraid of her. She told him she has no tail at all in human form, and admires his ("mine's a little softer"). At a 2.6 festival (limited event) she rewarded him for his courage, then proposed he model a woman's outfit for a publishing event. She says Kujou Sara did not inherit "daddy tengu's" brilliant mind and wishes Sara would stop pestering her with questions about Ei. Sara respects her because the Shogun trusts her.
